correctness.rationale: Friedman–Hoşten–Rosana Theorem 3.5 gives finite count [x^k] product_i(1+x^(s_i)) for the full Jordan partition. A finite discriminant critical set must have at least one size>=2 block, since diagonalizable repeated eigenvalues lead to infinity. Splitting a block a+b into a,b adds x^a+x^b coefficientwise, hence the largest possible coefficient occurs for partition (2,1^(n-2)), yielding binom(n-2,k)+binom(n-2,k-2), deficit 2binom(n-2,k-1). Complex symmetric N=[[i,1],[1,-i]] squares to zero and realizes the extremal block; direct sums with pairwise distinct eigenvalues meet the cited finiteness condition. n=2,k=1 correctly gives empty finite critical set. Independent exact small-n binomial/Jordan checks agree. The bound is mathematically correct.
